passage: The team restructuring was due on Friday, and the manager had asked Parveen to lead the new quality unit. Imran heard in the pantry that she'd said no again, the second promotion she'd turned down. He wasn't surprised. In three years he'd never heard her speak in a meeting, though half the fixes the team presented began in her notes. Monday night

Seema turned down the team lead role again today. Third time. In the meeting, when the manager announced it, she looked at the table the whole time. Afterwards I asked her why. She said, "I'm not leadership material. Others are more qualified."

I've sat next to her for two years. She's the one who fixed the billing error that saved the company from losing the biggest client. She trains every new joiner, patiently. In meetings she never speaks, but she sends the best ideas afterwards, by email, quietly.

I'm going to say something to her tomorrow. Not "you're great," she'll wave that away. Specific things. The billing fix. The new joiners. The emails.

I don't know if it will change her mind. But I think she doesn't see herself the way we see her.

— Reena
